conditions.name: Autism (ASD)
conditions.note: Morton 2023 reframed the ASD signal away from single taxa toward a gut-brain metabolic architecture — amino-acid / carbohydrate / lipid profiles encoded largely by Prevotella, Bifidobacterium, Desulfovibrio and Bacteroides, with glutamate the strongest metabolite signal. Counterweight (Neuron 2025): classifiers cannot separate autistic children from their own siblings, and stool consistency (constipation/diarrhoea) confounds many case-control ASD taxa findings — so treat the single-taxon directions below cautiously.

taxa.name: Bifidobacterium
taxa.refs: Aarts et al. 2017, PLoS One (PMID 28863139) vs. 2026 meta-analysis, 8 studies (PMID 40828192)
taxa.note:
Reduced in ADHD. A 2026 meta-analysis of 8 studies found the parent phylum Actinobacteria lower in ADHD children vs. neurotypical controls (5.78% vs 4.89%, p<0.001), and a separate 15-pair study found the phylum AND Bifidobacterium within it reduced - this app's own ADHD Actinobacteria entry records the same decrease.

SUPERSEDED CLAIM, kept for transparency: an older report (Aarts 2017) found Bifidobacterium INCREASED and proposed the dopamine-precursor story - more Bifidobacterium raising phenylalanine synthesis, a dopamine precursor. That study was small, used uncorrected p-values, and its own authors called the finding "marginally significant". It is recorded here rather than deleted, but it does not carry equal weight and the entry is not marked "both" - a single underpowered dissent is not equipoise.

Caveat that applies either way: stimulant medication is a plausible confounder none of these studies fully separate.

taxa.name: Lactobacillus
taxa.refs: Systematic review of gut microbiota and neuropsychological development in childhood and adolescence, ADHD arm n=7 studies (PMID 41868611); genus heterogeneity: PMID 32293557
taxa.note: LOOKED FOR, AND THE LITERATURE DOES NOT AGREE - which is different from nobody having studied it. A systematic review covering childhood and adolescent neuropsychological development found reduced Lactobacillus (with Blautia and Bifidobacterium) in AUTISM across 23 studies, but for ADHD, across 7 studies, 'findings were less consistent' - no direction survives. Recorded as contested rather than omitted so the map distinguishes 'inconsistent evidence' from 'no evidence'. A likely reason it scatters: 'Lactobacillus' held 261 species described as extremely diverse and was split into 25 GENERA in 2020, so studies either side of that split can be counting different organisms under one name (PMID 32293557). Expect this to stay contested until ADHD studies report at species level.

conditions.name: OCD
conditions.note: A 2023 systematic review (Law et al.) and a dysbiosis-centred review (Bendriss et al.) corroborate this profile: OCD shows LOWER gut α-diversity (species richness/evenness) and the recurring pattern of increased Alistipes (Rikenellaceae) alongside depletion of Prevotellaceae and butyrate producers (Oscillospira, Odoribacter, Anaerostipes, Agathobacter, Coprococcus, Lachnospira) — with Lachnospira pectinoschiza depletion tracking obsession-subscale severity. Direction isn't settled: a saliva/blood study found Actinobacteria and Firmicutes raised, and a natural-OCD deer-mouse model showed increased Desulfovermiculus, Aestuariispira, Peptococcus, Holdemanella and families Lachnospiraceae/Ruminococcaceae (animal — and opposite to the human Lachnospiraceae depletion). Probiotic signal: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and L. casei attenuate OCD-like behaviour in rodents; no human RCT yet. A 2021 JAMA Psychiatry transdiagnostic meta-analysis (59 case-control studies across 8 psychiatric disorders including both OCD and anorexia nervosa) found Coprococcus depletion as part of a shared cross-diagnostic pattern; this app's own data independently shows Alistipes (up), Agathobacter (down), Coprococcus (down), and Lachnospira (down) all moving the same direction in both OCD and anorexia nervosa — convergent, not contradictory, evidence.

conditions.name: FUT2 (Non-secretor)
conditions.note: Baseline host-genotype profile, not a diagnosis. HOW SOLID IS ANY OF THIS, read first: the effect is real but small, and whether you see it depends on method. Stool 16S found nothing in 1,503 UK twins (PMID 27871240), 35 adults (PMID 28358023), 350 mother-infant pairs (PMID 38838470) or exclusively breastfed infants (PMID 37741856). But the large genetic studies with species-level resolution do find FUT2 reproducibly — 12,652 people plus Nordic replication (PMID 41688637) and 7,738 in the Dutch Microbiome Project (PMID 35115690) — and whole-genome sequencing ties secretor status specifically to B. longum (PMID 29378630). Mucosal biopsies show a difference where stool does not (PMID 42355923), which fits the mechanism: FUT2 glycans are on the mucosa. Most individual arrows below still rest on 12-14 non-secretors, so read them as small-study signals. Non-secretors can't make the fucosylated oligosaccharides Bifidobacteria feed on — so Bifido runs low, and with it GABA. Non-secretor status is also linked in the literature to a wider set of conditions beyond gut bacteria: oral/dental (dental caries, periodontal disease, oral submucous fibrosis, precancerous oral lesions), gastrointestinal (peptic ulcers, Crohn's disease, necrotizing enterocolitis), genitourinary (vaginal candidiasis), and a strong genetic link to Type 1 Diabetes (nonsecretor A/A genotype confers susceptibility, OR=1.29, P=4.3×10⁻¹⁸, n=8,344 T1D cases) that isn't just genetic on its own — a 2020 mini-review (PMID 33425974) reports non-secretor children share the SAME low-Bifidobacterium/high-Bacteroides gut-microbiota signature as children with T1D itself, proposing FUT2-shaped early-life bifidobacteria colonization as a plausible mechanistic bridge between the two. See also this app's Type 1 Diabetes condition. Non-secretors also show a distinct infection-susceptibility PATTERN rather than uniformly "worse": protected from Norovirus, Rotavirus symptomatic infection, and H. pylori adhesion, but more susceptible to Cholera and (per the same review) low-level Candida/Streptococcus infections; secretors, conversely, show higher HIV progression risk and more severe respiratory viral illness (influenza). See linked citations below for each. Cognitive link worth flagging: Clostridiaceae — reduced in non-secretors (Kumar et al. 2015) — is one of only two bacteria this app links to Poor working memory (PMID 35010939, its depletion associated with worse working memory quality), so non-secretor status may plausibly extend to reduced working memory via this shared bacterial pathway, though this specific chain hasn't been tested directly in one study.

Corroborated in infants of non-secretor mothers, caesarean-born only (PMID 30214024). Dissent, outweighed: germ-free mice colonised from non-secretor-mother infants had MORE Akkermansia (PMID 38530054) — mouse, so the human data set the arrow.

links.label: Wacklin et al. 2014, PLOS ONE — 71 adults, HITChip (PMID 24733310)

Sci Rep 2019 (76 secretor vs 15 non-secretor mothers; in caesarean-born infants of non-secretor mothers bifidobacteria strongly depleted and Akkermansia lower; no effect in vaginally born; PMID 30214024)
Germ-free mice colonised from infants of non-secretor mothers 2024 (mSystems; higher Akkermansia/Enterocloster/Klebsiella, lower Bacteroides/Bifidobacterium/Blautia; PMID 38530054)

taxa.name: Blautia
taxa.refs: PMID 24733310; dissent: PMID 28710295; second dissent PMID 38530054
taxa.note: Blautia et rel. significantly higher in non-secretors (p<0.05), HITChip analysis. Dissent, outweighed: a 33-subject study (6 non-secretors) found Blautia higher in SECRETORS, the opposite direction - smaller, and only 6 people on the side that matters (PMID 28710295). Second dissent: those same mice had LOWER Blautia (PMID 38530054) — mouse, outweighed.

links.label: Wacklin et al. 2014, PLOS ONE — 71 adults, HITChip (PMID 24733310)
Germ-free mice colonised from infants of non-secretor mothers 2024 (mSystems; higher Akkermansia/Enterocloster/Klebsiella, lower Bacteroides/Bifidobacterium/Blautia; PMID 38530054)

taxa.name: Dorea
taxa.note: Dorea formicigenerans et rel. significantly higher in non-secretors (p<0.05), HITChip analysis. Rests on the 12-vs-12 deep-sequenced subset of PMID 24733310. Searched 2026-08: no second study reports this taxon by secretor status.

links.label: Wacklin et al. 2014, PLOS ONE — 71 adults, HITChip (PMID 24733310)

taxa.name: Ruminococcus gnavus
taxa.note: Ruminococcus gnavus et rel. significantly higher in non-secretors (p<0.05), HITChip analysis — distinct from the bare Ruminococcus genus, which showed no single clean direction and isn't tracked here for that reason. Rests on the 12-vs-12 deep-sequenced subset of PMID 24733310. Searched 2026-08: no second study reports this taxon by secretor status.

links.label: Wacklin et al. 2014, PLOS ONE — 71 adults, HITChip (PMID 24733310)

taxa.name: Bacteroides
taxa.note: B. plebeius et rel. and B. fragilis et rel. co-occurred specifically in secretors (implying lower abundance in non-secretors); consistent with an earlier study from the same group reporting higher Bacteroides diversity/abundance in secretors. Dissent, outweighed: a 33-subject study (6 non-secretors) found Bacteroides higher in NON-secretors, the opposite direction - smaller, and only 6 people on the side that matters (PMID 28710295).

links.label: Wacklin et al. 2014, PLOS ONE — 71 adults, HITChip (PMID 24733310)

taxa.name: Prevotella
taxa.note: One of five indicator OTUs (alongside unclassified Lachnospiraceae, Sutterella, Faecalibacterium) identified for healthy non-secretor individuals in an indicator-species analysis. DISSENT, recorded not resolved: in 19 post-bariatric-surgery patients, Prevotella increased among SECRETORS - the opposite direction. Small, and a heavily confounded population, so it does not overturn the finding; it does mean this arrow is no longer unopposed (PMID 32872099).

links.label: Rausch et al. 2011, PNAS — healthy + Crohn's cohort, indicator-species analysis (PMID 22068912)

taxa.name: Sutterella
taxa.note: One of five indicator OTUs (alongside Prevotella, unclassified Lachnospiraceae, Faecalibacterium) identified for healthy non-secretor individuals in an indicator-species analysis. SEARCHED, NOTHING FOUND: a targeted search for any other study of Sutterella against secretor status returns nothing. This arrow rests entirely on one indicator-species analysis inside an 18-person healthy subgroup, and no corroboration exists to find. Treat accordingly.

links.label: Rausch et al. 2011, PNAS — healthy + Crohn's cohort, indicator-species analysis (PMID 22068912)

taxa.name: Candida albicans
taxa.note: A 2022 review states non-secretors are "often more commonly related to low-level infections including yeast (Candida) and Streptococcus," and separately cites a case-control study finding non-secretor status predisposes to vaginal candidiasis (Kulkarni & Venkatesh 2004) and non-secretion of blood group antigens associated with susceptibility to Candida species infection (Thom et al. 1989).

links.label: Kaur et al. 2022, Int J Mol Epidemiol Genet — review (PMID 35892094)

taxa.name: Helicobacter pylori
taxa.note: Opposite pattern from most pathogens on this map: SECRETORS (not non-secretors) are more susceptible. Positive-BabA-adhesin H. pylori strains require the secretor phenotype's fucosylated glycans to adhere to and infect gastric epithelium in both humans and rhesus monkeys (Azevedo et al. 2008, J Pathol) — so non-secretors are relatively protected from this specific colonization route.

links.label: Kaur et al. 2022, Int J Mol Epidemiol Genet — review of Azevedo et al. 2008 (PMID 35892094)

taxa.name: Clostridiaceae
taxa.note: Family-level abundance decreased significantly more across pregnancy in non-secretors vs. secretors (p=0.05, n=123 pregnant women, 108 secretors/15 non-secretors); C. coccoides group counts specifically decreased more in non-secretors (qPCR, p=0.02), and Clostridium species richness was also reduced (DGGE). Study population is pregnant women specifically, not general population — noted as a caveat. This directly matters for cognition: Clostridiaceae is one of only two bacteria this app links to Poor working memory (its depletion associated with worse working memory quality, PMID 35010939) — so non-secretor status may plausibly extend to reduced working memory via this same pathway.

links.label: Kumar et al. 2015, PLoS One — 123 pregnant women, 108 secretors/15 non-secretors (PMID 26231005)

taxa.name: Firmicutes
taxa.refs: Wacklin et al. 2014, PLOS ONE - 71 adults screened, 24 sequenced (12 non-secretors / 12 secretors), pyrosequencing + HITChip (PMID 24733310)
taxa.note: Tested, no phylum-level difference. The study this app leans on most for FUT2 measured it directly: 'at the phylum level, the non-secretors, secretors and FUT2 genotypes shared similar microbiota compositions, dominated by Firmicutes (on average 93%)' - same result by HITChip (84%). WHY IT LOOKS OTHERWISE: several individual Firmicutes genera ARE higher in non-secretors in that same study - Clostridium, Blautia, Dorea, Ruminococcus gnavus and C. sphenoides - so the impression that 'non-secretors have more Firmicutes' is right about the members and wrong about the total. Non-secretors also had significantly lower diversity (p=0.001).

links.label: Wacklin et al. 2014 - no phylum-level difference by secretor status (PMID 24733310)

taxa.name: Eubacterium hallii
taxa.refs: Inferred source (evidence for the FEEDING RELATIONSHIP, not for this condition - nobody measured this taxon here): derived via cf_infantis_ehallii - Mol Nutr Food Res 2023 (PMID 36938958) | derived via cf_akkermansia_eubacterium_hall - Belzer et al. 2017, mBio - A. muciniphila co-cultured with A. caccae, E. hallii and F. prausnitzii (PMID 28928206)
taxa.note: FROM CROSS-FEEDING - inferred, not measured in this condition. Bifidobacterium is down here, and it feeds Eubacterium hallii (acetate, lactate, 1,2-propanediol -> butyrate), so Eubacterium hallii is expected to follow. Lower confidence - the reverse direction was not tested. The feeding relationship itself is real (in-vitro-coculture); its presence in THIS condition is an inference. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED: 2 separate feeding routes imply the same direction here - also Akkermansia -> Eubacterium hallii (mucus-derived oligosaccharides, acetate, 1,2-propanediol, in-vitro-coculture, cf_akkermansia_eubacterium_hall).

taxa.note: FROM CROSS-FEEDING - inferred, not measured in this condition. Bifidobacterium is down here, and it feeds Anaerostipes (lactate -> butyrate), so Anaerostipes is expected to follow. Lower confidence - the reverse direction was not tested. The feeding relationship itself is real (in-vitro-coculture); its presence in THIS condition is an inference. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED: 2 separate feeding routes imply the same direction here - also Akkermansia -> Anaerostipes (mucus-derived oligosaccharides, acetate, 1,2-propanediol, in-vitro-coculture, cf_akkermansia_anaerostipes).

links.label: Inferred source: Two routes of metabolic cross-feeding between Bifidobacterium adolescentis and butyrate-producing anaerobes (PMID 16672507)

taxa.name: Desulfovibrio
taxa.refs: Inferred source (evidence for the FEEDING RELATIONSHIP, not for this condition - nobody measured this taxon here): derived via cf_fprausnitzii_dpiger - Khan et al. 2023, Nature - co-isolated F. prausnitzii and D. piger, cross-feeding for growth and butyrate production (PMID 37532933)
taxa.note: FROM CROSS-FEEDING - inferred, not measured in this condition. Faecalibacterium prausnitzii is down here, and it feeds Desulfovibrio (lactate (as electron donor) -> acetate; supports D. piger growth), so Desulfovibrio is expected to follow. Lower confidence - the reverse direction was not tested. The feeding relationship itself is real (in-vitro-coculture); its presence in THIS condition is an inference.

links.label: Inferred source: Khan et al. 2023, Nature - co-isolated F. prausnitzii and D. piger, cross-feeding for growth and butyrate production (PMID 37532933)

conditions.name: Bipolar Disorder
conditions.note: Evidence base is smaller than for MDD; findings vary by mood state (depressed vs manic vs euthymic), by subtype (BD-I vs BD-II), and by medication (especially atypical antipsychotics, which independently shift the microbiome). Most primary cohorts sampled during a depressive episode. Common thread across studies: reduced α-diversity that scales with illness duration, and depletion of butyrate-producing Faecalibacterium/Roseburia/Coprococcus.

conditions.name: Borderline Personality Disorder
conditions.note: EVIDENCE BASE IS THIN. As of 2026, exactly one primary 16S study exists (Rössler 2022, n = 24 unmedicated BPD women vs 21 HC women — all-female cohort). Alpha- and beta-diversity did not differ between groups; the signal is at species level, in bacteria that produce or feed short-chain-fatty-acid pathways. Findings correlated with psychometric severity but have not yet been independently replicated. Male BPD, medicated BPD, and BPD with comorbidities (MDD, PTSD, eating disorders) are essentially unstudied. Treat everything here as directional, not established. The SCFA-depletion pattern is directionally consistent with what's seen in MDD, BD, and anxiety, which is unsurprising given the high comorbidity.

conditions.name: Parkinson's disease
conditions.note: The most robust, best-replicated gut-microbiome signal in neurology. The recurring pattern: mucin-layer-degrading Akkermansia up, SCFA/butyrate producers (Roseburia, Faecalibacterium, Lachnospiraceae, Blautia, Fusicatenibacter) down. Nishiwaki showed this holds across countries and is independent of constipation, BMI, sex, age and COMT-inhibitor use. Mechanistic throughline: butyrate loss + mucus-layer degradation → barrier permeability → enteric α-synuclein. Caveats: directions are for established PD; COMT inhibitors independently raise Lactobacillaceae, and disease stage shifts the picture (Faecalibacterium/Fusicatenibacter depletion predicts faster progression).

conditions.name: ME/CFS
conditions.note: Two simultaneous 2023 Cell Host & Microbe cohorts (Guo n=106/91; Xiong short- vs long-term). Core signal: loss of butyrate-producing capacity — F. prausnitzii and E. rectale depleted, with F. prausnitzii abundance inversely tracking fatigue severity, confirmed functionally by metagenomics, qPCR and fecal SCFA metabolomics. Xiong found dysbiosis pronounced in short-term (<4 y) disease but largely resolved in long-term (>10 y) patients who retained metabolic/clinical aberrations — so disease duration matters. Opportunistic species (R. gnavus, Enterocloster, Hungatella, Eggerthella) enriched.

conditions.name: Fibromyalgia
conditions.note: Well-controlled case-control (Minerbi 2019): 77 women with FM vs matched controls, with differences independent of diet, physical activity, medication and comorbid IBS, and taxa abundance tracking symptom severity. Signature is a reshuffle of the butyrate-producing community — the well-characterised 'healthy' producers (F. prausnitzii, B. uniformis, P. copri, Blautia faecis) depleted while less-characterised producers (Intestinimonas, Flavonifractor, Eisenbergiella, Butyricicoccus) rise, mirrored by altered serum SCFAs. Bifidobacterium and Eubacterium (neurotransmitter-metabolising genera) reduced — a plausible tie to the low-GABA / high-glutamate axis reported in FM.

conditions.name: PTSD
conditions.note: EVIDENCE BASE IS THIN — small, heterogeneous, mostly phylum-level, with no consistent α/β-diversity difference. Anchored by one exploratory study (Hemmings 2017, n=18 PTSD + 12 trauma-exposed controls). The recurring finding is depletion of Actinobacteria, Lentisphaerae and Verrucomicrobia (the last includes barrier-supporting Akkermansia), with depletion tracking CAPS-5 symptom severity. Later cohorts (Malan-Müller 2022, Zeamer 2023) add genus-level signals but overlap poorly, and several cohorts are veteran/occupational, limiting generalisation.

conditions.name: Anorexia nervosa
conditions.note: IMPORTANT — most of these shifts are downstream of the semi-starved, low-BMI state itself, not a cause. Methanobrevibacter smithii tracks inversely with BMI, faecal SCFA excretion falls on a hypocaloric diet, and several changes partially (though often incompletely) renormalise with weight restoration. The one causal signal is Fan 2023, where transplanting AN microbiota into germ-free mice transferred an anorexia-like phenotype — so the microbiome may also feed back onto the illness. Functionally, gut-brain modules for serotonin biosynthesis and for dopamine / glutamate / tryptophan degradation are enriched in AN, a plausible route to mood and appetite effects. Evidence is heterogeneous (small cohorts, few at species level, starvation a massive confound) — read the taxa as an illness-state signature, not a target. A 2021 JAMA Psychiatry transdiagnostic meta-analysis (59 case-control studies across 8 psychiatric disorders including both OCD and anorexia nervosa) found Coprococcus depletion as part of a shared cross-diagnostic pattern; this app's own data independently shows Alistipes (up), Agathobacter (down), Coprococcus (down), and Lachnospira (down) all moving the same direction in both OCD and anorexia nervosa — convergent, not contradictory, evidence.

conditions.name: Tourette syndrome
conditions.note: EVIDENCE IS THIN AND INCONSISTENT — small, paediatric tic-disorder (TD/TS) cohorts, mostly single-centre, with no consensus on α- or β-diversity and taxa that move in opposite directions across studies; treat directions as tentative. The most reproducible signals are increased Bacteroides and Ruminococcus (Ruminococcus lactaris especially enriched in TS specifically) and decreased Bifidobacterium. A GABA thread runs through the data and may interest you: the GABA-degrading Klebsiella pneumoniae rises with symptom deterioration, while GABA-producing Bifidobacterium, Eubacterium and Akkermansia muciniphila are inversely correlated with tic severity (YGTSS) — yet, oppositely, some GABA-producing Bacteroides species (B. thetaiotaomicron, B. eggerthii, B. dorei) correlate positively with severity. Notable conflicts: one drug-naive-TD cohort (Wang 2022) found Prevotella and Faecalibacterium INCREASED, opposite to the depletion seen in most other conditions here, and Odoribacter is up in TD but down in OCD. A probiotic/FMT signal exists (Limosilactobacillus reuteri; small FMT case series) but no definitive RCT.

conditions.name: Multiple sclerosis
conditions.note: Autoimmune demyelinating CNS disease. The flagship iMSMS shotgun study (576 patients + genetically unrelated household controls) is the strongest dataset: it reports enrichment of Akkermansia muciniphila, Ruthenibacterium lactatiformans, Hungatella hathewayi and Eisenbergiella tayi, and depletion of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Blautia. The recurring theme is loss of butyrate producers (Faecalibacterium, Roseburia, Coprococcus, Butyricimonas) plus a mucin-degrader (Akkermansia) and methanogen (Methanobrevibacter) rise. Composition also shifts with disease-modifying therapy, so treatment status is a major confound. See also this app's Lupus (SLE), Rheumatoid arthritis, Type 1 Diabetes, Crohn's disease, and Ulcerative colitis conditions — Faecalibacterium depletion specifically recurs across all of them.

taxa.name: Akkermansia muciniphila
taxa.note: Mucin-layer degrader; the most reproducible MS enrichment across cohorts. A lower Bifidobacterium(adolescentis):Akkermansia(muciniphila) ratio tracks higher EDSS disability (PNAS 2025). Note: some progression studies report Akkermansia falling in progressors, so within-MS direction is context-dependent. Cross-ref: also the single most consistent Parkinson's enrichment. A 2026 systematic review of 16 studies (2010-2023, nine countries) corroborates: "most publications reported... increased levels of A. muciniphila in MS patients compared to controls."

taxa.name: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii

A 2026 systematic review of 16 studies (2010-2023, nine countries) corroborates: "most publications reported decreased levels of F. prausnitzii... in MS patients compared to controls."

taxa.name: Blautia
taxa.note: iMSMS reports depleted Blautia species in MS; the MS-associated Blautia wexlerae drives inflammation and a lower Bifidobacterium:Akkermansia ratio in mouse transfer (PNAS 2025). Caveat: some reviews report Blautia ↑ in MS — direction is contested. Cross-ref: Blautia is ↓ in autism as well. Further reinforcing the contested picture: the largest MS microbiome meta-analysis to date (14 cohorts, n=1,493) found RRMS samples enriched in a Blautia-dominated enterotype, i.e. pointing up, not down.

taxa.name: Eisenbergiella tayi
taxa.note: Enriched in MS (iMSMS shotgun). Cross-ref: Eisenbergiella (incl. E. tayi and E. massiliensis) is also ↑ in fibromyalgia (Minerbi) and rises in rodent learned-helplessness depression models — a recurring 'up' signal across pain / neuro-inflammatory conditions. Upgraded from correlational to causal evidence by a 2025 PNAS study: ileal microbiota from the MS-affected twin in identical-twin pairs induced EAE (the standard MS mouse model) at substantially higher rates than microbiota from the healthy co-twin, and E. tayi (with Lachnoclostridium) was specifically identified as one of the likely active, disease-triggering organisms.

conditions.name: Ehlers-Danlos (hypermobile)
conditions.note: Heritable connective-tissue disorder (defects in collagen / ECM). Gut involvement is real and common — chronic GI symptoms in ~80% — but it is a story of dysmotility, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) and overlap with IBS/POTS/MCAS, NOT a characterised fecal taxon signature. There is currently no validated microbial biomarker for hEDS, so the entries here are deliberately sparse and flagged as indirect. Included because Kelsey's rheumatologist context makes the EDS/hypermobility axis relevant and because it cross-links strongly to IBS and fibromyalgia.

taxa.name: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO)
taxa.note: Not a single taxon — overall small-bowel bacterial load. In hypermobility disorders (including hEDS) with GI symptoms, ~70% meet SIBO criteria on aspirate (≥10^3 CFU/mL); 100% of those with gastroparesis or dyssynergic defecation. Mechanism is connective-tissue-driven dysmotility allowing luminal microbes to proliferate, not a distinctive dysbiotic community.

links.label: Hypermobility SIMD study 2026 (aspirate + breath test; SIBO prevalence)

taxa.name: Reduced microbial diversity
taxa.note: hEDS has no validated stool taxon signature. The literature is dominated by dysmotility/SIBO and very heavy overlap with IBS and functional foregut disorders (up to ~98% of hEDS patients meet criteria for a disorder of gut-brain interaction). Diagnostic microbial biomarkers have not been established — treat any species-level claim for EDS as provisional.

conditions.name: Irritable bowel syndrome
conditions.note: Disorder of gut-brain interaction; the most-studied gut condition here and a natural comparator for the neuropsychiatric set (IBS is highly comorbid with depression, anxiety, fibromyalgia, autism and hEDS). Pittayanon 2019's systematic review anchors the signature: ↑ Enterobacteriaceae, Lactobacillaceae and Bacteroides; ↓ uncultured Clostridiales I, Faecalibacterium (incl. F. prausnitzii) and Bifidobacterium. Diversity is decreased or unchanged. Subtype (IBS-C/D/M) matters — e.g. methanogens rise in constipation-predominant disease — and most studies cannot cleanly separate subtypes.

conditions.name: Endometriosis
conditions.note: Estrogen-dependent inflammatory disease (endometrial-like tissue outside the uterus); frequently comorbid with IBS. Two microbiomes matter — gut and reproductive tract — and the 'estrobolome' (gut microbes that deconjugate estrogens via β-glucuronidase) is the proposed mechanistic link. Gut findings (this atlas' focus): a higher Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio, phylum-level rises in Actinobacteria/Proteobacteria/Verrucomicrobia, loss of Lactobacilli and butyrate producers (Ruminococcaceae, Lachnospira), and severity-dependent shifts (Dialister ↓, Streptococcus/Lactobacillus ↑ with stage; Prevotella/Bacteroides ↓ in advanced disease). Directions are frequently contested between Shan 2020, Svensson 2021 and the 2025 meta-analysis, so several taxa here carry explicit caveats. See also this app's Estrogen condition, which tracks the same estrobolome mechanism from the opposite direction — bacteria correlated with circulating estrogen level generally, rather than this entry's endometriosis-specific dysbiosis pattern. Field-level caveat (2025-2026): a 36-study scoping review concluded there is no reproducible gut dysbiosis profile in endometriosis — the largest shotgun study, once corrected for multiple testing, found nothing — and an FDR-corrected Mendelian randomization of 119 genera left no genus standing. Read every arrow below as an association from small cohorts.

conditions.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
conditions.note: The Prevotella copri expansion is the single most-replicated finding in RA gut-microbiome research, first shown in new-onset untreated patients and since reproduced in mouse models of arthritis susceptibility. See also this app's Lupus (SLE) condition — Faecalibacterium (a primary butyrate producer) is reported depleted across both, part of a broader pattern this app also tracks in Multiple sclerosis, Type 1 Diabetes, Crohn's disease, and Ulcerative colitis.

taxa.name: Akkermansia muciniphila
taxa.note: One of the more consistent findings — increased in psoriasis/psoriatic arthritis, an interesting contrast to its 'protective' role in metabolic disease. conditions.name: Type 1 Diabetes
conditions.note: Genetically linked to FUT2 non-secretor status: the nonsecretor A/A genotype of rs601338 confers T1D susceptibility (OR=1.29, 95% CI 1.20–1.37, P=4.3×10⁻¹⁸ across 8,344 T1D cases, 10,008 controls, 3,360 T1D families) — the authors describe "an intriguing relationship between host resistance to infections and susceptibility to autoimmune disease." Bacteria taxa below are from a separate, direct gut-microbiome case-control study — and the overlap isn't just genetic: a 2020 mini-review reports non-secretor children share the SAME gut-microbiota signature as children with T1D (both show fewer bifidobacteria and more Bacteroides), the exact Bifidobacterium-down/Bacteroides-up pattern this app's own T1D taxa list below already shows, and proposes FUT2-shaped early-life bifidobacteria colonization as a plausible mechanistic bridge. See also this app's Non-secretor (FUT2) condition.

taxa.name: Parabacteroides distasonis
taxa.note: ANIMAL MODEL, not human data — recorded because the mechanism is unusually specific. P. distasonis carries an insB9-23 mimic in its hprt protein, and colonising female NOD mice induced severe insulitis via molecular mimicry, activating insB9-23-specific T cells and accelerating diabetes onset. Notably targeted: it did NOT shift overall microbiome composition, metabolite profiles, or general immune activation, and heat-inactivated bacteria had no effect — so live organisms selectively activating diabetes-relevant autoimmunity, rather than broad inflammation. Human relevance untested.

conditions.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
conditions.note: Affects an estimated 8-13% of women of reproductive age — one of the most common endocrine disorders in women, and historically under-researched relative to its prevalence. Gut dysbiosis in PCOS is characterized by reduced alpha-diversity (Shannon SMD=-0.27, phylogenetic diversity SMD=-0.39) and a shift favoring pro-inflammatory taxa. Several taxa below show genuine cross-study contradictions (marked "both") rather than a single clean signature — reflected honestly rather than picked a side. See also this app's Estrogen and Testosterone conditions: PCOS is defined by both estrogen dysregulation and hyperandrogenism (elevated testosterone), and several taxa there (Collinsella, Sutterella, Subdoligranulum, Paraprevotella, Akkermansia) are drawn from PCOS-specific cohorts.

conditions.name: Premenstrual Disorders (PMS/PMDD)

conditions.name: Menopause (transition)
conditions.note: Host life-stage entry, not a disease state. Large, well-powered shotgun-metagenomic cohort (n=1,322 total) found menopause-associated microbiome shifts toward a profile more similar to men's, plausibly related to declining estrogen/progesterone (the "estrobolome" — gut bacterial genes that metabolize estrogens). Associated with adverse cardiometabolic risk profile; associations held after adjusting for cardiometabolic confounders. See also this app's Perimenopause condition (the fluctuating-hormone phase before this sustained-low-estrogen state) and its Estrogen and Progesterone conditions (the specific hormones whose decline this life-stage entry reflects).

conditions.name: Perimenopause
conditions.note: Host life-stage entry, not a disease state — the fluctuating-hormone transition period BEFORE menopause proper, distinct from the sustained-low-estrogen postmenopausal state this app tracks separately as "Menopause (transition)." A 2022 review specifically distinguishes the two phases: perimenopause shows reduced Lactobacillus/Bifidobacterium and increased Enterobacter, while postmenopause instead shows a broader shift toward a male-like profile. The 3 taxa entries here rest on one review's characterization (not yet an independently-replicated primary cohort the way the postmenopausal entry has); the wider link list below situates that claim among the broader menopausal-transition microbiome literature rather than leaving it isolated. See also this app's Estrogen and Progesterone conditions — the specific fluctuating hormones this transitional phase is named for.

conditions.name: Estrogen
conditions.note: Host hormone-level entry, not a disease state — tracks the "estrobolome": gut bacteria whose abundance correlates with circulating/urinary estrogen or estrogen-metabolite levels in human cohort studies. This is a genuinely emerging, smaller-sample, exploratory research area compared to most other conditions in this app — several source studies explicitly caution their own taxon-level findings should be treated as exploratory, and that caveat is preserved here rather than smoothed over. Complements this app's separate Menopause (transition) and Perimenopause entries, which track the reciprocal, better-powered question (what changes about the microbiome as estrogen declines) rather than this one (what correlates with estrogen level directly). See also this app's PCOS and Endometriosis conditions — both are fundamentally estrogen-driven. Taxa sourced ONLY from disease-specific subpopulations (e.g. a PCOS-only cohort) rather than a healthy/general population or a direct hormone-level correlation are deliberately excluded here, since the goal of this entry is estrogen's own effect, not PCOS's — see the Sutterella entry below for a case where that distinction reverses the finding entirely.

taxa.note: CORRECTED (was previously listed as 'up', sourced only from a PCOS-only obese-women cohort — that finding is confounded by PCOS status, not a clean read on estrogen alone, and has been dropped). The direction here is inferred instead from this app's own Menopause (transition) data: Sutterella wadsworthensis is consistently reported ENRICHED in low-estrogen postmenopausal women vs. higher-estrogen premenopausal women (PMID 35675542), a finding a 2026 review of estrogen/gut-microbiome physiology reaffirms (PMID 41978103). If low estrogen tracks with more Sutterella, higher estrogen should track with less — the opposite of the discarded PCOS-only claim. This is a cross-referenced inference, not a direct estrogen-dosing study of Sutterella — flagged as such rather than presented as equally strong as this entry's directly-measured taxa.

conditions.name: Testosterone
conditions.note: Host hormone-level entry, not a disease state — tracks the emerging "testobolome" concept (a testosterone-metabolism analogue to the estrobolome): gut bacteria whose abundance correlates with serum testosterone. Taxa sourced only from disease-specific subpopulations (male type 2 diabetics, PCOS-vs-healthy group comparisons) were removed from this entry after an audit — those cohorts' findings are confounded by the disease itself, not a clean read on testosterone alone (see this app's Estrogen entry's Sutterella correction for a case where this exact confound flipped a finding's direction). What remains here is either a healthy-cohort serum-level correlation, or a genus-level correlation computed across a whole mixed sample against continuous hormone level (a legitimate way to isolate the hormone's own association) rather than a disease-status comparison. A landmark 2013 Science study in GERM-FREE MICE (Markle et al., PMID 23328391) showed this relationship can run causally in both directions — transferring male gut microbiota into female mice raised their testosterone — flagged explicitly here as a mouse mechanistic finding, not a human correlation, but included because it's the strongest evidence this is a real bidirectional pathway and not just a marker. See also this app's PCOS condition — hyperandrogenism (elevated testosterone) is one of PCOS's hallmark diagnostic features.

conditions.name: Progesterone
conditions.note: Host hormone-level entry, not a disease state. Genuinely thinner evidence base than this app's Estrogen or Testosterone entries - a 2022 systematic review searching specifically for sex-hormone/gut-microbiota associations (PMID 35283442) found NO direct progesterone-taxon abundance correlations in the literature it covered, only a passing mechanistic note about butyrate. What real evidence does exist is more mechanistic than correlational: a landmark 2024 Cell paper identified specific bacterial species that metabolically PRODUCE progestins from host glucocorticoids (a genuinely different kind of relationship than "this bacterium's abundance rises with progesterone," flagged per-taxon below), plus one solid human pregnancy cohort finding for Bifidobacterium specifically. Kept honestly small (3 taxa) rather than padded to match the other hormone entries' counts - the link list below is intentionally broader than the taxa list, since most of what's citable here is context/mechanism rather than new per-genus findings. See also this app's Premenstrual Disorders (PMS/PMDD) condition and this app's PMDD brain-map entry — PMDD is fundamentally a progesterone-withdrawal-sensitivity condition, this hormone's strongest clinical link in this app — and its Menopause (transition)/Perimenopause conditions, since progesterone declines alongside estrogen through that transition.

conditions.name: Lupus (SLE)
conditions.note: New condition, added after a user question about how broadly F. prausnitzii/butyrate-producer depletion is reported across autoimmune disease specifically flagged lupus as missing from this app. Two independent, directly-verified sources: a 2024 scoping review of human+animal controlled studies from 2013-2023, and a 2025 case-control study of active vs. stable SLE vs. healthy controls (16S rRNA, n=65 total). A specific 'X% of studies' figure for this pattern was asked about directly but could not be independently verified in any source actually checked — not included here rather than guessed at.
